podcast.title: On-Stage Headphones
podcast.body: Brad Delson is known for wearing large, "clunky set of headphones" on stage, which were reportedly designed by Mike Shinoda. While Delson has never provided a direct explanation for wearing them, it is speculated they serve as monitors to ensure he can hear the band clearly during live performances. "Guitarist Brett Delson appears on stage wearing a big clunky set of headphones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: UCLA Enrollment
podcast.body: Brad Delson attended UCLA, where he became roommates with Dave "Phoenix" Farrell, who would later become Linkin Park's bassist. "Brad enrolled in UCLA, where he became roommates with a bass player named Dave Phoenix Farrell."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Origin in Agoura Hills
xref.body: The core of Linkin Park began with three high school friends—Mike Shinoda, Brad Delson, and Rob Bourdon—who attended Agoura Hills High School, located approximately 30 miles northwest of downtown Los Angeles. "Everything with his band starts at a high school in Agora Hills, which is about 30 miles northwest of downtown Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Band Formation
xref.body: Relative Degree was the first musical group in which Brad Delson and Rob Bourdon played together, preceding their formation of Super Zero with Mike Shinoda. "Brad and Rob were the first to play together in a group called Relative Degree."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Headphone Designer
xref.body: Mike Shinoda reportedly designed the distinctive "big clunky set of headphones" often worn on stage by Linkin Park guitarist Brad Delson. "Mike Xionota apparently designed them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Precursor to Zero
xref.body: Super Zero was the band formed by Brad Delson, Rob Bourdon, and Mike Shinoda after their previous group, Relative Degree, disbanded. Its name was later shortened to "Zero" (spelled Xero). "When they broke up, they found Mike and Ford have called Super Zero, which was eventually shortened to just zero and spelled with an X, by the way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Temporary Departure from Hybrid Theory
xref.body: In 1999, Farrell temporarily left Hybrid Theory to tour the Christian circuit with his former band, Tasty Snacks. This absence necessitated the hiring of two session bass players for Linkin Park's debut album, *Hybrid Theory*, with Brad Delson filling in for any unplayed parts. "Didn't help that Dave, the bass player, left a tour of the Christian circuit with Tasty Snacks that year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
